title: streamed-visibility-delta-metrics-and-privacy-gates-for-toolcall-boundaries
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Add delta-oriented per-slice metrics and trace span boundaries specifically aligned to tool/function-call boundaries in streamed responses, while enforcing a pluggable redaction/privacy gate for all streamed logs and telemetry. Goal: enable product and infra teams to answer questions such as 'what fraction of token slices trigger external tool calls', 'per-slice latency for toolcall vs generator-only slices', and 'KV cache hit distribution across slices' without leaking PII from streamed content. This ticket covers instrumentation, sampling strategy, redaction hooks, compatibility with legacy streaming protocol, and rollout plan.
technical_notes: Instrument runtime to emit 'slice' metrics: slice_id, seq_in_request, source (generator|toolcall), kernel_profile, kv_cache_hit {true|false}, token_count, slice_latency_ms
Trace integration: create a span per slice with parent span = request root; add tags for toolcall_id when slice crosses a tool boundary; ensure spans can be stitched after out-of-order arrival

Redaction: implement a redaction pipeline that runs before any telemetry leaves the edge stack; support redact-levels = [none, basic, strict]; strict removes any substrings matching high-sensitivity regexes and replaces with stable placeholders

Sampling: default 100% for internal requests, 5% for customer traffic; sampling adjustable via per-customer config in Console; sampled slices should still emit a low-cardinality 'sampled' metric to estimate total counts

Compatibility: provide a compatibility shim for older SDKs that expect a single streaming channel; shim will synthesize per-slice metrics based on reconstructed boundaries inferred from token markers; annotate shim-created metrics with 'compat_mode=true'
Storage: metrics aggregated to Prometheus histograms and per-customer ingest to ClickHouse for ad-hoc queries; ensure no raw slice content is stored in long-term stores
Performance: add minimal path instrumentation (atomic counters + fast path buffer) to keep p95 slice instrumentation overhead < 1%)
acceptance_criteria: Create per-slice latency and token-count histograms in Prometheus with label set {customer, model_family, region, source, kv_cache_hit}
Runtime emits a tracing span per slice and spans are visible in our tracing backend with stable slice_id tags
Redaction pipeline prevents PII from appearing in logs or traces for a 3rd-party generated test corpus (see design doc for corpus) under 'strict' mode
Compatibility shim produces metrics annotated with compat_mode=true and does not alter customer-facing streaming payloads
Dashboard: Console dashboard 'Streaming → Slice Insights' with default panels for toolcall rate, slice latency by source, and KV hit ratio is created
Rollout: feature gated behind 'slice_observability_v2' with canary enabled for 5% of internal orgs, no customer-visible errors at canary scale for 72 hours
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike complete — implemented a microbench for slice span emission; observed 0.6% p95 overhead for 128-token windows on rtx-a10g nodes
2026-02-15: Design review with privacy team — accepted redact-levels model; privacy requested added unit tests and corpus-based validation
2026-02-18: Implemented initial compat shim for legacy streaming SDKs; validated with SDK integration tests; shim annotates metrics with compat_mode=true
2026-02-22: First end-to-end test: traces link slice spans to request root; created synthetic test that simulates interleaved toolcalls and generator slices
2026-02-25: QA found edge case where slices spanning toolcall boundaries get double-counted in token histograms; working on dedupe using canonical slice_id assignment
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High-cardinality tags from freeform tool names could blow up metric cardinality. Mitigation: whitelist tool names and map unknown names to 'tool:other' before emitting metrics
Risk: Redaction false positives could remove critical debug tokens. Mitigation: redact at telemetry boundary but store hashed fingerprint in a separate internal-only field for debugging when approved
Risk: Compatibility shim may mis-guess boundaries. Mitigation: mark shim metrics with compat_mode and run reconciliation job comparing shim metrics with native instrumentation on canary traffic
Risk: Increased network/ingest cost. Mitigation: default low sampling for customer traffic and allow per-customer overrides
deployment_plan: Step 1: Merge runtime instrumentation behind feature flag 'slice_observability_v2'
Step 2: Deploy to staging and enable for internal orgs only; run telemetry validation tests
Step 3: Roll out canary to 5% internal orgs for 72 hours; run reconciliation job between shim and native metrics
Step 4: Enable for 5% customer orgs with default sampling=5%; monitor error budget and telemetry pipeline backpressure
Step 5: If stable, accelerate to 25% then 100% with migration notes for customers relying on legacy dashboards
Rollback: flip feature flag off and sweep ephemeral metrics; ensure no persistent storage of raw slices occurred
qa_steps: Run end-to-end harness that interleaves three toolcalls per request and ensures slice spans are present and stitched
Validate redaction using the privacy corpus under all redact-levels; assert no PII remains in logs/traces
Load test at 2x expected production throughput and measure instrumentation overhead and ingest cost
Verify compat shim metrics are annotated and that reconciliation reduces metric divergence below 3% before broad rollout
